courses.title: Multiprocessor Programming Techniques
courses.description: The main objective is obtaining the necessary skills on using specific techniques for multiprocessor programming.
courses.objectives:
The main objective is obtaining the necessary skills on using specific techniques for multiprocessor programming.
After taking this course, students will be able to :
- Explain notions specific to multiprocessor programming: theoretical conceps like consistency models or guarantees (linearizability,
sequential consistency, wait-freedom, lock-freedom), various synchronization mechanisms (types of locks, barriers, etc.), data structures
specifically optimized for concurrent access (lists, queues, stacks, etc.), advanced aspects (parallelism in publish/subscribe systems)
- Design and implement application modules optimized for using multiple cores
- Use advanced techniques for multiprocessor programming in at least one programming language (Java)
courses.topics_lecture:
Introduction. Basic notions recap – from mutual exclusion to
producer/consumer and readers-writers. Specific guarantees in
multiprocessor programming the importance of parallel execution
(Amdahl’s law).
Concurrent execution – general concepts. Deadlock-freedom vs.
Starvation-freedom in the context of mutual exclusion. Brief
introduction of the Java memory model.
Concurrent objects – general concepts. Consistency models:
sequential consistency, linearizability. Progress conditions: wait-
freedom, lock-freedom.
Locks – I. General aspects. The contention factor. TAS lock vs.
TTAS lock. Queue-based locks: the Anderson lock.
Locks - II. Advanced versions: the CLH lock, the MCS lock.
Lists with concurrent access - I. General aspects. Variants: coarse-
grained, fine-grained, optimistic synchronization.
Lists with concurrent access - II. Variants: lazy synchronization,
non-blocking synchronization. Comparison of list versions.
Recapitulative verification.(*) Homework presentations.
Queues and stacks with concurrent access I. Variants: partial
bounded queue, lock-free unbounded queue.
Queues and stacks with concurrent access II. The ABA problem.
The lock-free unbounded stack.
Concurrent hashing. Variants: closed-address (lock-based and lock-
free), open-address.
Specific techniques for parallel processing I. Concepts: work and
critical path. The scheduler impact. Work stealing and work dealing
techniques. MapReduce – introductory discussion. Parallel
processing of data streams.
Specific techniques for parallel processing II. Work stealing and
work dealing. Advanced aspects: MapReduce, parallel processing of
data streams – introductory discussion.(*)
Barierrs.
Introductory discussions on programming using transactional
memory – general aspects.(*)

courses.description: 7.1 General Objective
courses.objectives:
7.1 General Objective
Acquiring of basic knowledge and skills in ethical academic and work related research endeavors
7.2 Specific Objectives
O1. Knowing the principles and standards enforced through national and international ethical codes of conduct and research
O2. Knowing the principles and standards enforced through international normative policies in regards to AI development
O3. Knowing the most common ethical problems related to digital technologies development
O4. Critical risk analysis in regards to emergent technologies development, with specific focus on social justice issues

courses.competencies:
 Studentul/Absolventul descrie într-o manieră coerentă principalele teorii etice și explică noțiunile generale ale domeniului,
referitoare la principiile fundamentale ale eticii academice, normele de integritate, tipurile de comportamente academice
inadecvate (plagiat, fals intelectual etc.) și la cadrul legal și instituțional privind etica în mediul universitar.
 Studentul/Absolventul identifică și analizează critic dileme etice specifice mediului academic, este capabil șă aplice în mod
corect regulile de citare și redactare științifică, să promoveze practici academice oneste și transparente în activitățile de studiu și
cercetare și este capabil să expliciteze ce înseamnă a avea un comportament moral din perspectiva diferitelor teorii etice.
 Studentul/absolventul aplică un cadru etic în utilizarea AI, cu responsabilitate față de impactul social al soluțiilor propuse.
 Studentul/Absolventul: 1. Are un comportament etic și responsabil în procesul de învățare și cercetare și respectă normele
deontologiei profesionale. 2. Gândește nuanțat și apreciază diversitatea perspectivelor și punctelor de vedere asupra moralității,
exersează și cultivă permanent modestia intelectuală și are înclinația de a-și revizui opiniile și convingerile în lumina dovezilor.
3. Acționează într-o manieră autonomă și integră în situații care presupun luarea unor decizii cu implicații etice.

courses.description: General Objective
courses.objectives:
General Objective
To enable students to acquire the basic techniques for designing programs in a procedural language.
Specific Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
O1. Explain how a program written in C works, including introductory elements of C++.
O2. Use algorithms and implement them in C/C++.
O3. Analyze a program written in C/C++.
O4. Describe data structures in C, including introductory elements of C++, suitable for developing an application.
O5. Develop a software application as part of a team.
O6. Calculate the execution time and memory requirements for running a program written in C.

6. Objectives
General Objective To understand the main concepts in Logic, as applied in Computer Science.
Specific Objectives:
After successfully passing the exam, the students will be able to:
- identify and build syntactically correct formulae;
- translate propositions from natural language to propositional logic or first-order logic;
- explain the difference between propositional logic and first-order logic;
- reason semantically about the satisfiability/validity of a formula and about semantical consequences/equivalences;
- use deductive systems such as resolution and natural deduction for mechanical proofs.
7. Specific competencies/Learning outcomes
 Studentul/absolventul alege, explică și specifică fundamentele matematice aplicate în informatică, inclusiv logica formală,
algebra, probabilitățile și statisticile.
 Studentul/absolventul aplică, evaluează, propune metodele matematice pentru modelarea, simularea și rezolvarea problemelor
informatice.
 Studentul/absolventul dezvoltă soluții interdisciplinare prin integrarea matematicii cu domenii conexe și colaborarea eficientă cu
echipe de specialitate.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Building a professional image with regards to the process of developing IT products. Students will learn advanced methods and
courses.objectives:
Building a professional image with regards to the process of developing IT products. Students will learn advanced methods and
techniques for creating complex, high quality programs while adapting to clients requirements regarding function, costs and deadline.
On successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
• Explain how to use object oriented programming principles in large development projects
• Describe the steps required to successfully implement a project for a client and describe the steps necessary for testing the project
• Utilize Java technologies to implement and test functional components of a given project
• Analyze customer requirements, analyze software errors that occur during the development of the project, analyze the manual tests on a
system
• Calculation of time, staffing and money needed to develop the project requested by the client

associations and relevant employers in the corresponding domain
IT companies from Iaşi and elsewhere in the country use software engineering techniques in the development of large scale projects. The
steps necessary for developing large applications (requirements engineering, modeling, implementation, integration, testing, deployment)
are widely discussed throughout the course, and students learn the basics and actually go through these stages. During the summer
students participate in internships in companies where they are involved in real projects where apply the theoretical concepts learned
during the course in real projects. Following discussions with major employers, this course is updated from year to year, adapting to the
current needs of the IT market and beyond.

first 6 laboratories and at least 50 % of the maximum projrct points)
Minimum exam score: the exam is not mandatory, but whoever takes the exam must obtain at least 40% of the maximum score that can
be obtained on the exam, otherwise it will be considered failed.
10.4 Minimum performance standard
Students will be able to identify the main requirements following the discussion with the client and will be able to model the solution that
the client expects. The implementation will be reduced to building the main classes and their attributes, without implementing the basic
methods. They will be able to test the project from the point of view of automatic and manual testing.
Minimum laboratory score: 50% of the maximum score that can be obtained in the laboratory without bonuses (minimum 50% of
laboratory assignments and minimum 50% project)
Minimum exam score: the exam is not mandatory, but whoever participates in the exam must obtain at least 40% of the maximum score
that can be obtained in the exam, otherwise it will be considered failed
For students who meet the promotion criteria, the final grade is established by dividing the score obtained by the maximum score without
bonus, and the result is multiplied by 10.
If one of the promotion criteria is not met, the student will obtain a grade less than or equal to 4.

courses.competencies:
Professional Skills
Upon successful completion of this discipline, students will be able to:
Explain how to create a 3D model or a character, how to rig it with bones and joints, and then animate it to create the desired movement;
how to create a 3D environment and simulate a dynamic scene.
Describe procedural modeling techniques and the roles played to generate complex 3D-models or natural environments.
Correctly use the principles of modeling (polygonal modeling, spline/NURBS modeling, surface modeling), create realistic materials, UV
map and unwrap the models, create animations for objects and characters.
Analyze how to visualize and communicate an idea, analyze real world movement and lighting scenarios to create a well-grounded
content.
Write code in Python to extend Blender’s animation capabilities.
Transversal Skills
Upon successful completion of this discipline, students will be able to:
Combine tools and techniques from different programs to create an entire 3D animated scene.
Develop add-ons in Python to extend modeling or animation capabilities.
Use different modeling, texturing, animation, lighting and rendering techniques and appropriate algorithms to create complex dynamic
scenes in procedural software products as Blender, Maya, 3ds Max, Cinema 4D, or Houdini.

6. Objectives
To put forward a background which catalysis and bring forward through experiment the creativeness and scientific association among
mathematics & computer science on one side and, visual arts & architecture on another - relationship inspired by bioscience/natural
sciences.
Acquiring basic knowledge / skills in the field of 3D modeling and animation; developing useful applications in the gaming industry,
medicine, architecture, forensics, education.
General objectives:
Understanding the fundamental principles of 3D animation – motion, time, space, and visual perception;
Developing algorithmic thinking in a visual context – applying programming and mathematical concepts to generating animations;
Familiarity with the tools and software environments specific to 3D modeling and animation;
Combining visual art with technical programming skills to create interactive and realistic animated scenes.
Specific objectives (knowledge):
Understanding the notions of 3D modeling, texturing, lighting, and rendering;
Explaining how the 3D graphics pipeline works;
Mastering the concepts of 3D geometric transformations (translation, rotation, scaling);
Understanding the principles of basic physics applied to animation (gravity, collision, motion);
Understanding interpolation algorithms, direct and inverse kinematics, and procedural simulation;
Knowledge of character and object modeling concepts, ranging from realistic and structurally accurate styles to cartoon styles; knowledge
of the principles of generating, simulating, and visualizing complex real-world processes associated with phenomena that have random
evolutions to create realistic environments; knowledge of methods for applying techniques and algorithms that give characters a full range
of emotions, or simulations of crowd behavior.

Professional Skills
Upon successful completion of this discipline, students will be able to:
Explain how to create a 3D model or a character, how to rig it with bones and joints, and then animate it to create the desired movement;
how to create a 3D environment and simulate a dynamic scene.
Describe procedural modeling techniques and the roles played to generate complex 3D-models or natural environments.
Correctly use the principles of modeling (polygonal modeling, spline/NURBS modeling, surface modeling), create realistic materials, UV
map and unwrap the models, create animations for objects and characters.
Analyze how to visualize and communicate an idea, analyze real world movement and lighting scenarios to create a well-grounded
content.
Write code in Python to extend Blender’s animation capabilities.
Transversal Skills
Upon successful completion of this discipline, students will be able to:
Combine tools and techniques from different programs to create an entire 3D animated scene.
Develop add-ons in Python to extend modeling or animation capabilities.

scenes in procedural software products as Blender, Maya, 3ds Max, Cinema 4D, or Houdini.

courses.description: Presentation in a simple and easy-to-understand manner of the essential concepts for building a scalable web application, based on the
courses.objectives:
Presentation in a simple and easy-to-understand manner of the essential concepts for building a scalable web application, based on the
principles of object-oriented programming.
Fundamental and advanced concepts from the .NET Core ecosystem will be explored, with a focus on:
- Databases: SQL Server and SQLite – differences, use cases, integration with .NET applications.
- Entity Framework Core – object-relational mapping, migrations, performance and best practices.
- Vertical Sliced Architecture – a modern and modular approach to organizing code.
- CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) – clear separation between city and writing operations for scalability and
maintainability.
Applying a coherent architectural pattern within the .NET Core Framework, with a concrete and easy-to-follow example.
The goal is to clearly understand how these technologies and principles combine to create robust, extensible and easy-to-maintain
applications.

courses.objectives:
7. Specific competencies/Learning outcomes
 Explain advanced concepts in Machine Learning
 Accurately describe certain advanced Machine Learning algorithms
 Use/apply these algorithms on different datasets
 Analyze the results of applying these algorithms
8. Contents
8.1 Course Teaching methods Remarks
(number oh hours,
references)
Revision of basic notions in probabilities and statistics: random Lecture 2 hours
events, probability function / distribution, the independence of
random events; random variabiles (discrete vs continuous ones), the
independence of random variabiles. Expectation and variance.
Common probabilistic distributions. Some basic [theoretical]
properties.
Introductory notions of Machine Learning. Lecture 2 hours
Main types of Machine Learning algorithms: classification,
clusterization, regression, ranking, feature selection,
recommendation systems.
Decision trees. The ID3 algorithm. Evaluation measures for Lecture 2 hours
classification algorithms: accuracy, training error, [cross-]validation
erorr, precision, recall etc.
Variants / extensions to the ID3 algorithm. Overfitting. Pruning Lecture 2 hours
strategies for decision trees.
Types / classes of hypotheses in Machine Learning: Maximum Lecture 2 hours
Likelihood (ML) hypotheses and Maximum A posteriory
Probability (MAP) hypotheses.
Bayesian classification. The Naive Bayes and Joint/Optimal Bayes
algorithms.
Computing the mean error rate for Bayesian classifiers. Lecture 2 hours
The nature of the decision boundary in Bayesian classification.
Parameter estimation for [uni-variate] probabilistic distributions: the Lecture 2 hours
MLE și MAP methods. The case of Bernoulli [and gaussian
univariate] distributions.
8.1 Course Teaching methods Remarks
(number oh hours,
references)
Revision. Partial exam 2 hours
Logistic Regression. Lecture 2 hours
The relationship between Bayesian classification and logistic
regression.
Instance-based learning. The k-nearest neighbour (k-NN) algoritm. Lecture 2 hours
The relationship between the asymptotic error rate of the 1-NN
algorithm and the error rate of the Joint Bayes algorithm.
Ensemble methods based on decision trees: the AdaBoost algorithm. Lecture 2 hours
Supervised learning (classification) vs unsupervised learning Lecture 2 hours
(clusterization). Main types of clustering algorithms. Hierarchical
clustering: aglomerative (bottom-up) vs divisive (top-down). Types
of similarity functions (single-link, complete-link, average-linkage,
Ward's metric).
Partitional clustering (i.e. non-hierarchical clustering using ”hard” Lecture 2 hours
assignment of instances to clusters): the K-means algorithm.
The monotonicity of the „distorsion” (J) criterion at the application Lecture 2 hours
of the K-means algorithm.

courses.title: Social Media Networks Analysis
courses.description: General Objective
courses.objectives:
General Objective
Acquiring basic knowledge in extracting static and dynamic data from various media sources, analyzing and interpreting the flow of
information distributed through social media networks. The methods proposed to be studied are based on mathematical and computational
models, built on concepts inspired by the fields in which they have wide applicability: social and political sciences, economics and
marketing, journalism, legal sciences, medicine, biology.
Specific Objectives
Knowing, understand and design mathematical and computational models on social media network; identify and discover complex,
dynamic, and evolution patterns using machine learning and data mining approaches or multi-agent-based simulation; construction of
social media network infrastructure
Knowing, understand and employ: social media network search algorithms (large-scale graph algorithms); security and privacy
techniques in social media networks (data protection inside communities); spatio-temporal characteristics in social media networks
(dynamics and evolution patterns).
Knowing, understand and use of modern statistical methods in social network analysis.

courses.competencies:
Professional Skills
Upon successful completion of this discipline, students will be able to:
C1. Explain how to extract information from social media.
C2. Describe how to bring together different types of data, from different sources; how to use different approaches to store data in ways
that allow fast and reliable exploration and analysis.
C3. Correctly explore data and communicate results so that data can be turned into interpretable, actionable information.
C4. Analyze social media networks with the aim to identify connections, influencers, and social roles.
Transversal Skills
Upon successful completion of this discipline, students will be able to:
C1. Combine methods and algorithms for extracting data in different formats and analyze information from various social media sources.
C2. Develop simulations that can be used to explore the processes that take place on an existing network (to anticipate the effects of
changing network structure on a complex system, or to predict problems).
C3. Use algorithms and programming techniques that facilitate the data networks analysis in their surrounding context.
